harper (docs): Heads-up: I found an inconsistency in the /v1/generate API ref. The param is shown as `timeout` (seconds) in the examples but the OpenAPI schema and SDKs use `timeout_ms` (milliseconds). Some customers copy the curl snippet and get 1000x shorter timeouts. I'll open a docs PR to clarify and add migration snippets.
samir (api): Good catch. Runtime accepts both for backwards compat, but we standardized on `timeout_ms` internally. Plan: update OpenAPI to document both fields (one preferred), mark `timeout` as deprecated, and add note about units. We'll also return a response header X-Timeout-Used for debugging.
ella (sdk): JS SDK currently accepts `timeoutMs` (camelCase) and validates as number ms. I'll add a compatibility shim that will accept `timeout` (seconds) and convert to ms with a dev-warning. Also mirror examples in docs for curl/python/js.
chad (prod-eng): Rationale: ms is more precise especially for low-latency routes; but many quickstarts used seconds. We should provide explicit examples: 30s -> timeout:30 vs timeout_ms:30000 and show both curl + JS + Python.
harper (docs): Draft snippets below — please confirm exact payloads so SDK tests match. I'll add a migration guide section titled "Timeout parameter units (seconds -> milliseconds)" and a short FAQ "Why did my request time out faster than expected?"
harper (docs): ```bash
# canonical curl (preferred: timeout_ms in ms)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"Write a summary","timeout_ms":30000}'
```
harper (docs): ```bash
# legacy curl example (seconds) - supported but deprecated
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"Write a summary","timeout":30}'
```
harper (docs): ```javascript
// js snippet - SDK accepts timeoutMs (preferred) and maps legacy timeout (s) -> ms
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
// preferred
await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1.0', input: 'Write a summary', timeoutMs: 30000 });
// legacy callers may pass timeout (seconds) - SDK will convert and warn in dev
await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1.0', input: 'Write a summary', timeout: 30 });
```
harper (docs): ```python
# python snippet - requests style, prefer timeout_ms
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_KEY'))
resp = c.generate(model='redwood-1.0', input='Write a summary', timeout_ms=30000)
# legacy: timeout (seconds) still accepted: timeout=30
```
ella (sdk): I'll implement the shim in JS SDK v1.6.0 and add unit tests that copy the curl/payload examples. I'll log a DeprecationWarning in dev builds when `timeout` is present. Also will ensure the SDK sends `timeout_ms` over the wire.
samir (api): When you update OpenAPI, add description: "timeout_ms (preferred) — request timeout in milliseconds. timeout (deprecated) — request timeout in seconds; provided for backwards compatibility. Server prefers timeout_ms if both present." Add example responses showing header X-Timeout-Used: 30000.
ci-bot: docs preview build queued.
chad (prod-eng): Small ops note: the runtime change adding X-Timeout-Used header will be rolled out in staging tomorrow and prod Friday 01:00-02:00 UTC. Coordinate SDK release same day.
harper (docs): Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/8888 (WIP) — changes: update API ref param docs, add canonical and legacy examples, add migration guide and FAQ, update OpenAPI examples.
ella (sdk): I'll link the SDK PR in the docs PR when ready. Also adding a changelog entry: "Docs: clarify timeout units; SDK will accept legacy `timeout` (s) and convert to `timeout_ms` (ms)."
ci-bot: docs preview build passed - preview: https://deploy-preview-8888--docs.redwood.ai/ (CI: ✔)
harper (docs): Thanks everyone. I'll merge after SDK patch lands and the X-Timeout-Used header is visible in staging requests. Will announce in #support with copy/paste migration snippets.
